Hi Alexandra — thanks for the clear list. Tagging Ben (runtime + identity) and Laura (private deploy product) to provide the specifics you asked for. High level answers below; Ben/Laura will follow with config snippets and logs mapping.

- Recommended pattern: Short-lived service principals via JIT SCIM provisioning is our preferred path for operator/service access in private control plane deployments. It reduces blast radius and aligns with our automated rotation and TTL enforcement. We do support pre-provisioned IdP service accounts as a fallback if customers need long-lived artifacts for existing automation.

- Key rotation: Control plane accepts dual active signing keys for a configurable overlap window (default 7 days). We can extend that per contract for enterprise customers — please state the required window in your runbook.

- Audit fields: We emit SAML NameID, assertion subject, service_principal_id (internal SP GUID), externalId (from SCIM), and the IdP issuer. Full list and an example auth-event JSON will be sent by Ben.

I'll get a concrete plan and sample SAML assertion + SCIM patch examples attached in the next message.

Best,

Alexandra / team — attaching a couple artifacts and a short-tech plan below. I included the minimum fields we require for JIT provisioning and the recommended assertion checks.

Attachment stubs: saml-assertion-sample.xml, scim-reconciliation-script.sh, redwood-jit-sp-diagram.png

Summary plan (high level):
- Flow: Operator authenticates at customer IdP (Okta) -> SAML assertion to Redwood control plane SP endpoint (private CP endpoint in VPC) -> Control plane validates assertion audience/issuer/signature -> If user/externalId not known, trigger SCIM POST to customer's SCIM endpoint (JIT) to request provisioning -> Customer SCIM responds with user/servicePrincipal object containing externalId and role claim -> Control plane maps to internal service_principal_id and issues short-lived runtime credential (30m default TTL).

- Assertion checks (MUST):
  * signature valid against configured IdP keys (supporting RSA and ECDSA)
  * Audience matches the private CP SP URL (we support multiple SP audience aliases for multi-region)
  * NotBefore / NotOnOrAfter tolerance: default skew 120s, configurable
  * Required attribute: Subject or NameID, Email (if present), and a custom claim 'x-rw-role' (optional but recommended)

- SCIM requirements (for JIT provisioning):
  * Endpoint: HTTPS POST /scim/v2/ServicePrincipals (we will send an HTTP Basic or mTLS token depending on your security team preference)
  * Schema: externalId (string), displayName, roles (list of role names), meta.sourceId, groups (optional)
  * Error handling: 409 -> we will attempt a PATCH flow, 429/5xx -> exponential backoff + alert to oncall (we can also route to a manual approval queue if you prefer)

- Certificate rotation: control plane accepts up to 3 active signing keys in the IdP config; keys are identified by KeyID. Rotation process: you push new key to Okta, add to our IdP config via API, wait N hours while both keys active, then remove old key. We log both the key used and the KeyID in auth events.

I'll paste a sanitized auth-event example in the next message along with the saml sample.

Notes on reconciliation: our scim-reconciliation-script.sh (attached) performs a daily delta: compares externalId -> if multiple matches found we flag for manual review; if none found we create; if matched but role differs we PATCH. We keep reconciliation logs in the control plane audit bucket for 90 days by default (can be extended).
